name: Czech
modelReview: built 2026-11-13 by Claude Fable 5.2 from usage notes written in Czech with no knowledge of cron, a rule book derived from them, the lexicon and the visible paradigms, after two schedule reads and five blind fluency reads of the rows and seven author passes; the renderer was built by an agent that saw no other renderer and no held-out row: 153 of 153 held-out rows passed on the first judged run. One hard-case row contradicted its rule and was corrected (four years are a list). The forms of the last author pass, about thirty places where the rule book was silent and the builder chose a general rule, and the built output beyond the rows have had no independent read; no blind recovery has been run. After the build one stutter was found and repaired test-first («vždy 1. dne v měsíci vždy 20 minut po…»), and rows were added for the code no row had reached; a sweep of 19,000 patterns in the family that broke Italian (two cadences together in one field) found no wrong schedule. Minutes, seconds, hours at one minute and days of the month that are runs and cadences together (more than seven values, at most three parts) are said as their parts (2026-11-13, no independent read yet). Also 2026-11-13: a cadence of five hours or more beside several minutes is said as a cadence, and more than six clock times no longer each become a window of seconds (they had been said one by one, up to fifteen); no independent read yet. The maintainer (Czech, not a native speaker) ruled from what they have seen in use that the short style's capitalised table forms («Po až Pá») are normal; 2026-11-13: says when both day fields must match (a day field written from a star beside a restricted one, as in Vixie cron), in rows, rule and renderer written by Claude Sonnet 5.5 from this rule book's seed and reviewed by Claude Fable 5.2; a blind Sonnet reader told these sentences from the union's 16 times of 16, and none has had a blind fluency read; 2026-11-14, by Claude Opus 5.5 on the maintainer's rulings: hours that tile the day are said bare («každé 2 hodiny», with no «denně» and no clock window or list), from a later start inside the first step by their start only («každé 2 hodiny od 1:00»), and with hours taken out as the bare cadence and «kromě»; a cadence that does not tile keeps both ends; minutes and seconds beside such hours are said after the cadence, apart from it («každé 2 hodiny, vždy 30 minut po celé hodině», «každých 6 hodin, vždy po dobu jedné hodiny každou minutu»); the bracketed series after a cadence of days or years («(1., 4., 7. a tak dále)», «(2028, 2032, 2036 a tak dále)») is gone. The rule book was amended and every affected row rewritten by hand before the renderer changed; nothing was blind-read and none of the new forms has had an independent read; also 2026-11-14, by Claude Opus 5.5: the clock-digit brackets after a place in the hour («(:00–:29)», «(:05–:55)», «(:45)», «(:29)», «(:29:00–:29:59)») are gone everywhere, and a from–to of places now ends in «včetně», which was the one thing the bracket said that the words did not; minute 0 among pieces is «v každou celou hodinu», no longer «0 minut po celé hodině» (found by the sweep, fixed test-first). Rows rewritten by hand before the renderer; nothing blind-read; also 2026-11-14, by Claude Opus 5.5 on the maintainer's rulings: a stretch of minutes over a step of two hours that tiles the day is said by the even or odd hours («každou minutu v sudých hodinách», «každou minutu v prvních 30 minutách každé sudé hodiny»), longer steps keep «vždy po dobu jedné hodiny»; minute 30 beside such hours is «v půl» («každé 2 hodiny v půl»). Rows by hand before the renderer; nothing blind-read. 2026-11-14: the weekday nearest a day («15W», «1W», «LW») is said in the short form the maintainer approved (see answers 5.7)
